In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the nuclear equation of state in asymmetric nuclear matter.
the understanding of the properties of nuclear matter at supra-saturation densities and at large asymmetries.
the study of the equation of state (EOS) of nuclear matter at high baryon density and low temperatures, which are the conditions prevailing at the early stages of the core collapse of a massive star.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are compatible with a moderate symmetry energy slope, L= 50±10 MeV, at normal density.
isospin diffusion is well described by transport models with a density dependent symmetry energy, and that stopping phenomena are not yet well understood.

the data from the LASSA experiment, together with those of the Chimera collaboration, provide a strong evidence for an increase of the symmetry energy with density, with the value of 35 MeV at normal density and a slope of 50 MeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the symmetry energy is stiffer than the predictions from most of the available models.

we are able to constrain both the symmetry energy slope at normal density and the isospin diffusion coefficient in the region of the nuclear surface, and that we have found evidence that isospin equilibration is not achieved in the most central collisions.
we have been able to provide new information on the density dependence and isospin diffusion properties of the nuclear symmetry energy in the nuclear density region around saturation density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion of nucleons in heavy-ion collisions is a powerful tool to probe nuclear matter equation of state, especially in the region of high densities.
the isospin diffusion process is not yet understood, and that it is not possible to extract the symmetry energy from the measured data.
the diffusion of isospin degrees of freedom is a powerful probe of the density dependence of symmetry energy, which is one of the least known properties of nuclear matter.
